toOrderDto in order-dto.ts is the only Order-to-DTO mapping and is used by every order use case

parsedVerdict.reasoning: All eight files in src/application serve one concern: use cases for order fulfilment and stock, plus a shared DTO file and one shared helper. Every use case that loads an order by id calls the single helper requireOrder (require-order.ts), so the not-found rule lives in one place. Order mapping always goes through toOrderDto (order-dto.ts). Stock rules are delegated to the domain functions reserveStock and releaseStock, and order-state validation to isOrderState. No file copies them. Persistence goes only through the OrderRepository and ProductRepository ports; no file uses a database, ORM or query client directly. Minor points that don't break the rule: place-order-use-case.ts and cancel-order-use-case.ts both build a product-by-id map inline, which is repeated plumbing, not a copied rule. list-stock-levels-use-case.ts maps stock levels inline, but it is the only place that does so. StockLevelDto sits in order-dto.ts, a naming nit only. No candidate flags were raised.
